def figureOutUdt(path):
		"""
		Iterates through the tag path and figures out if any UDT
			instances are in the path. If a UDT instance was
			found in the path, then retrieves the list of alarms
			from the top UDT definition found in the path and
			returns them.
			
		Args:
			path: The path of the tag being searched.
			
		Returns:
			False if no UDT instances were found in the tag path, or a
			list of alarms from the top UDT definition in the path if
			a UDT instance is found in the path.
		"""
		
		# extracting the tag provider from the tag path, and getting
		# each 'part' of the tag path and storing it in a list:
		# [provider]this/is/an/example, provider='[provider]', 
		# and pathParts=['this','is','an','example']
		pathParts = path.split(']')
		provider = pathParts[0] + ']'
		pathParts = pathParts[1].split('/')
		parentPath = provider
		
		# starting from the beginning of the tag path, going to see if there
		# are any udt instances in the tag path: example path:
		# [default]test 1/testInstance/test/New Instance/testing, 'test1'
		# is a folder, 'testInstance' is a udt instance, 'test' is a folder 
		# inside testInstance, 'New Instance' is a udt instance, 'testing' 
		# is a memory tag; the type of 'testInstance' is 
		# '[default]_types_/mydefs/more/parent' and the type of 'New Instance' 
		# is '[default]_types_/child'; in this example with a nested udt, we 
		# need to get the config of 
		# '[default]_types_/mydefs/more/parent/test/New Instance/testing'
		for i in range(0,len(pathParts)):
			parentPath = parentPath + pathParts[i] + '/'
			config = system.tag.getConfiguration(parentPath[:-1])[0]
			if str(config['tagType']) == 'UdtInstance':
				# we have a udt instance, so we will get the udt type path; from the
				# example, at this point, parentPath = '[default]test 1/testInstance'
				udtParentType = str(system.tag.read(parentPath[:-1]+'.UDTParentType').value)
				start = i + 1
				definitionPath = provider + '_types_/'+ udtParentType + '/'
				# from the example, udtParentType ='mydefs/more/parent', start = 2
				# definitionPath = [default]_types_/mydefs/more/parent/, because
				# we need to get config of 
				# '[default]_types_/mydefs/more/parent/test/New Instance/testing',
				# we need to append '/test/New Instance/testing' to definitionPath
				for start in range(start,len(pathParts)):
					definitionPath = definitionPath + pathParts[start] + '/'
				# from the example, definitionPath = '[default]_types_/mydefs/more/parent/test/New Instance/testing'
				# if there is a key called 'alarms' in the config, then the alarm list will be returned, otherwise
				# an empty list will be returned		
				defConfig = system.tag.getConfiguration(definitionPath)[0]
				if 'alarms' in defConfig.keys():
					return defConfig['alarms']
				else:
					return []
				break
		
		# no udt instance found in the above loop	
		return False	
	

	logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.lg.config')
	
	# if the tag path is not empty, see if there is a udt instance in the path,
	# and if there is, store the udt alarms in the udtDefAlarms custom prop
	if value != '':
		udtDefAlarms = figureOutUdt(value)
		if udtDefAlarms != False:
			logger.debug('the selected tag is located within a udt instance; tagpath= ' + str(value))
			# when storing this info in perspective properties, the period/dot character is considered invalid if it is in a key
			# so, voip.customMessage needs to be changed to voip_customMessage
			for alarm in udtDefAlarms:
				if 'voip.customMessage' in alarm.keys():
					alarm['voip_customMessage'] = alarm['voip.customMessage']
					del alarm['voip.customMessage']
					
			self.custom.udtDefAlarms = udtDefAlarms
		else:
			self.custom.udtDefAlarms = []
			
		logger.debug('loading tag configuration; tagpath= ' + str(value))
		tagConfig = system.tag.getConfiguration(value)[0]
		
		# this resource is only used for editing alarms, so
		# it is not necessary to store tag attributes other
		# than the tag name, tag path, and the 'alarms'
		for key in tagConfig.keys():
			if key not in ['alarms','name','path']:
				del tagConfig[key]
		
		logger.debug('alarms, name, path of tag configuration= ' + str(tagConfig))
		
		if 'alarms' in tagConfig.keys():
			alarms = tagConfig['alarms']
			logger.debug('tag contains ' + str(len(alarms)) + ' alarms; tagpath= ' + str(value))
			
			# when storing this info in perspective properties, the period/dot character is considered invalid if it is in a key
			# so, voip.customMessage needs to be changed to voip_customMessage
			for alarm in alarms:
				if 'voip.customMessage' in alarm.keys():
					alarm['voip_customMessage'] = alarm['voip.customMessage']
					del alarm['voip.customMessage']
			
			tagConfig['alarms'] = sorted(alarms, key=lambda k: k['name'])
		
		self.custom.loadedTagConfig = tagConfig
		return tagConfig
	else:
		logger.debug('tag path empty')	
	
		self.custom.udtDefAlarms = []
		self.custom.loadedTagConfig = {}
		return {}

# when the selected tag changes from either the small view or
	# the large view, this updates both the 'tag' custom property,
	# which holds the tag path of the tag, and the selection data
	# of the tag tree (so that if the breakpoint switches between
	# the large view and the small view, the tag tree will still
	# have the correct selection data)
	
	# because a new tag has been selected, clear out the custom 
	# properties that are passed down to the binding editor in
	# the lg and sm version (the binding editor may have been
	# open when the user decided to select a different tag
	# outside of the binding editor, so need to make sure that
	# it is closed)
	
	self.view.custom.propName = ''
	self.view.custom.displayName = ''
	self.view.custom.alarmProp = {}
	
	path = payload['path']
	selections = payload['selections']
	
	self.view.custom.tag = path
	self.view.custom.selection = selections[0]
	self.view.custom.selectionData = selections[1]

# when the selectedRow of the alarm list changes from either the small view
	# or the large view, this updates the selectedRow custom property
	
	self.view.custom.selectedRow = payload['row']

def findAlarmIndex(alarmList,name):
		"""
		Utilizes the alarm name to find the row index of the
			alarm in the alarm list.
		
		Args:
			alarmList: List of alarms for this tag.
			name: Name of the alarm being searched.
		
		Returns:
			If the alarm name was found in alarmList, then
			the index of the alarm is returned. If the
			alarm name was not found in alarmList,
			then -1 is returned.
		"""
		for i, alarm in enumerate(alarmList):
			if alarm['name'] == name:
				return i
		return -1
	
	# when an alarm property is modified from either the small view or the large view,
	# this applies the change to the alarm object locally (in the tagConfig object)
	
	logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.propchange')
	logger.debug('alarm property modified; payload= ' + str(payload) + '; tag path= ' + self.view.custom.tagConfig['path'])
		
	propName = payload['propName']
	propVal = payload['propVal']
	
	selectedRow = self.view.custom.selectedRow
		
	# either an associated data property removed or a binding on a non-associated data property removed
	if 'noBinding' in payload.keys() or 'delete' in payload.keys():
		del self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow][propName]
	
	# associated data property name changed
	elif 'adNameChange' in payload.keys():
		# propName is the old name, and propVal is the new name
		currVal = self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow][propName]
		del self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow][propName]
		self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow][propVal] = currVal
			
	else:
		# name of an alarm changed
		if propName == 'name':
			alarms = list(self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'])
			singleAlarm = dict(self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow])
			singleAlarm[propName] = propVal
			alarms[selectedRow] = singleAlarm
			newAlarms = sorted(alarms, key=lambda k: k['name'])
			self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'] = newAlarms
			
			# the row index of this alarm may be different after changing the alarm name,
			# so, will try to update the selected row
			alarmIndex = findAlarmIndex(newAlarms,propVal)
			if selectedRow != alarmIndex:
				self.view.custom.selectedRow = alarmIndex
			
		else:
			# basic alarm property change
			self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow][propName] = propVal

# the 'overridden' text has been pressed, meaning that the user wants the current
	# selected alarm to have the same props as the UDT definition alarm; the
	# 'udtAlarm' param passed to this message handler holds the UDT definition alarm;
	# so, we set the current selected alarm equal to the UDT definition alarm
	
	logger = system.util.getLogger('configurator.overridden')
	logger.debug('overridden text has been pressed to revert alarm back to UDT def; payload= ' + str(payload) + '; tagpath= ' + self.view.custom.tagConfig['path'])
	
	selectedRow = self.view.custom.selectedRow

	udtAlarm = payload['udtAlarm']
	self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][selectedRow] = udtAlarm

# when a new alarm is added on the large view or the small view, the new
	# sorted list of alarms (containing the new alarm) is passed to this
	# message handler; then, the 'alarms' list for the tagConfig custom
	# property is updated
	
	self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'] = payload['alarms']

# when an alarm is removed from the small view or the large view, the name
	# of the alarm is passed to this message handler; then, once we find the
	# alarm in the tagConfig, we can remove it
	
	name = payload['name']
	
	tagConfig = self.view.custom.tagConfig
	for index,alarm in enumerate(tagConfig['alarms']):
		if alarm['name'] == name:
			del self.view.custom.tagConfig['alarms'][index]

# this message handler is called either from the 'commit' button
	# or the 'revert' button to refresh the binding on tagConfig
	
	self.view.refreshBinding('custom.tagConfig')

# in order to maintain the state of the tag tree between the large view and
	# the small view (in terms of which folders/UDT instances are expanded), this
	# message handler is called to update the 'items' custom property (holds the
	# current state of the items for the tag tree) whenever the items prop of the
	# tag tree changes (the items prop of the tag tree changes when opening and
	# closing folders/UDt instances)
	
	self.view.custom.items = payload['items']

# when the binding editor needs to be opened or closed, this message handler
	# is called; if the length of propName is not greater than 0, then the
	# binding editor is not displayed
	
	propName = payload['name']
	prop = payload['prop']
	displayName = payload['displayName']
	
	self.view.custom.displayName = displayName
	self.view.custom.propName = propName
	self.view.custom.alarmProp = prop
